text:
Decided to consolidate the per-room photoresistor onto the presence sensor ESP32-C3, so each room has one device instead of a presence ESP plus a D1 Mini running light_sensor.yaml. Not built yet.

Agreed so far: the MQTT topic stays zigbee2mqtt/sensors/<room>/illuminance, so nothing downstream changes.

Still unanswered when we pick this up:
- Whether the office currently runs light_sensor.yaml on a D1 Mini. If it does, that device has to be decommissioned at the same time, or two publishers fight over the same illuminance topic.
- Whether other rooms use light_sensor.yaml, which decides if the file stays in the repo.

Constraints found while scoping it, which are easy to get wrong:
- Usable ADC on the ESP32-C3 is ADC1 only, GPIO0 to GPIO4. GPIO3 and GPIO4 are the LD2410 UART and GPIO2 is a strapping pin, so the divider goes on GPIO0 or GPIO1. ADC2 (GPIO5) does not work while Wi-Fi is up under ESP-IDF.
- The 'return x * 100.0;' lambda in light_sensor.yaml is correct only on ESP8266, where ESPHome reports 0 to 1.0 V. On the C3 you need 'attenuation: 12db' and a full scale near 3.3 V, so copying that line unchanged gives readings up to about 310.
- Rejected wiring the photoresistor between two GPIOs with one driven high as the supply. It saves power the mains-powered board does not need, and adds series resistance to a divider whose output impedance already peaks near 9.5k with a 10k fixed resistor, at the edge of what the C3 ADC handles cleanly.
- Open risk: the radar's best mounting spot may not see representative room light. The user judged it acceptable but this was not measured.

calibrate_ld2410.py talks to the presence sensor through the ESPHome web server (REST + SSE) only. MQTT was rejected because the script would need broker secrets and MQTT writes give no status; the native API was rejected because presence_sensor.yaml has no api: block and adding one means a reflash. The script is a phone-driven local web app on 0.0.0.0:8765 by user request, so the user can run it from outside the room. It has not yet been run against a real LD2410; all verification was against a fake device, so the SSE JSON shape for switches and the echo timing after a number write are assumptions. Reviewer findings about polling-dependent failure detection, fresh-echo verification and worker coordination on shutdown were deliberately rejected as overbuilt for a single-phone tool; do not reopen them without a real failure.

calibrate_ld2410.py has now run against the real LD2410 (2026-09-13). First real run got through connect, entity discovery, engineering mode on, and the SSE stream, so the switch JSON shape and stream handling assumptions in gavtue held. It failed at the end of the empty phase because ESPHome gate energy sensors dedup and only publish on change; fixed by seeding each phase's maxima from the last published value (see comment in start_phase). The echo timing after a number write is still unverified on real hardware.
The calibrate_ld2410.py page is used on both a phone and a desktop browser, so layout must work at about 360 px and 720 px. User wants dark mode only; light mode was offered and declined.

Real hardware (2026-09-13) showed the write verification in calibrate_ld2410.py was too weak for Timeout / Max Move / Max Still: ESPHome's set_max_distances_timeout echoes the number instantly, restarts the LD2410 module 200 ms later and re-reads all parameters ~1 s after. Writes sent during that restart are lost and the re-read reverts the echoed value (max still stayed 8 while max move landed 7). Fixed by sleeping MODULE_RESTART_SECONDS after each of those three writes and re-verifying. This supersedes the 'fresh-echo verification is overbuilt' rejection in gavtue for these three numbers only; gate threshold writes do not restart the module and were fine.

calibrate_ld2410.py moved out of this repo on 2026-09-13 to its own public repo, github.com/skorokithakis/ld2410-calibrator (AGPL-3.0). The ld2410-calibration entries here describe its history; new work on the tool happens there.
